headline: Tanzid Hasan Tamim scores first Test century on Australian soil
summary: The opener's maiden Test ton helps Bangladesh extend their lead to 88 runs over Australia in the opening Test at Marrara Stadium.
details: Opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim struck 101 off 197 balls, becoming the first Bangladeshi batter ever to score a Test century on Australian soil.
Tanzid's maiden Test ton included eight fours and a six, before he was caught at long-off by Mitchell Starc off Nathan Lyon's delivery.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto also contributed with a strong innings, reaching 79 runs as Bangladesh continued to dominate the second day of the match.
By tea on Friday, Bangladesh reached 286 for three, extending their lead to 88 runs over Australia's first innings total of 198.
Tanzid and Mominul Haque shared a crucial 102-run partnership for the second wicket, while Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim added 55 runs for the fourth wicket.
Australia's full-strength side used six different bowlers, including Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood, to contain the Tigers.
With Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das still to come, Bangladesh is in a strong position as the pitch is expected to become better for batting as the day progresses.
caption:
History made in Darwin! Tanzid Hasan Tamim becomes the first Bangladeshi to score a Test century in Australia.

Opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim struck 101 off 197 balls, becoming the first Bangladeshi batter ever to score a Test century on Australian soil.

Tanzid's maiden Test ton included eight fours and a six, before he was caught at long-off by Mitchell Starc off Nathan Lyon's delivery.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto also contributed with a strong innings, reaching 79 runs as Bangladesh continued to dominate the second day of the match.

By tea on Friday, Bangladesh reached 286 for three, extending their lead to 88 runs over Australia's first innings total of 198.

Tanzid and Mominul Haque shared a crucial 102-run partnership for the second wicket, while Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim added 55 runs for the fourth wicket.

Australia's full-strength side used six different bowlers, including Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood, to contain the Tigers.

With Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das still to come, Bangladesh is in a strong position as the pitch is expected to become better for batting as the day progresses.

headline: Gold prices cut by 2,158 taka per bhori after three hikes
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has reduced the price of 22-carat gold, bringing it down to 234,621 taka per bhori.
details: The price of gold in the domestic market has decreased on Friday, August 14, following three consecutive price increases.

According to a notice from the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS), the price of the highest quality 22-carat gold has been reduced by 2,158 taka per bhori, setting the new price at 234,621 taka.

The new rates, which became effective from 10:00 AM on Friday, also apply to other categories: 21-carat gold is now 224,065 taka, 18-carat gold is 192,398 taka, and traditional method gold is 157,172 taka per bhori.

While gold prices have fallen, the prices of silver remain unchanged. 22-carat silver is currently 5,074 taka, 21-carat is 4,841 taka, 18-carat is 4,199 taka, and traditional method silver is 3,149 taka per bhori.
